MG5 Case Summary & Antecedents 
- Prosecution relies on witness ID, partial CCTV, partial DNA, medical. 
No comment interview.   
- Antecedents: minor, non-violent (theft 2019, public order 2021, 
cannabis 2022); no violence/weapons history. 
 
--- 
 
## 17 MG6C Unused Material Schedule (Incomplete) 
- Phone data (pending), additional CCTV (pending), clothing forensics 
(pending), PNB entries (partial), medical records (not obtained). 
Defence requests completion, forensic and phone disclosure, full 
continuity. 
 
--- 
 
## 18 Disclosure Correspondence (Highlights) 
- Defence (20 Aug): requests complete MG6C, CCTV continuity, phone data 
clarity, full forensic methodology/chain, medical mechanism 
clarification, timetable.   
- CPS (25 Aug): acknowledges; working to complete by 01 Sep; continuity 
and phone reliance pending.   
- Defence follow-up (28 Aug): presses for completion by PTPH (04 Sep); 
will seek directions if not met. 
 
--- 
 
## 19 Defence Review & Strategy 
- **Primary Strategy:** Fight Charge (Trial Strategy) — challenge 
identification reliability under Turnbull; if identification fails, 
case collapses. Charge reduction (s18 → s20) remains fallback if 
identification is admitted but intent is contestable.   
- **Pressure Points:** Turnbull ID risk 
(lighting/hood/duration/uncertainty); CCTV quality insufficient for 
facial ID; medical single-motion ambiguity; brief duration (15–30s); 
partial/non-exclusive DNA; incomplete MG6C; continuity gaps 
(CCTV/weapon); phone data pending.   

- **Win Conditions (Fight Charge):** Identification successfully 
challenged/excluded under Turnbull; prosecution case collapses; OR 
identification admitted but intent not proven beyond reasonable doubt; 
medical supports single/brief blow; CCTV shows no sustained/targeted 
conduct; weapon use lacks targeting/duration.   
- **Win Conditions (Charge Reduction Fallback):** If identification 
admitted, then: no s18 intent articulated beyond reasonable doubt; 
medical supports single/brief blow; CCTV shows no sustained/targeted 
conduct; weapon use lacks targeting/duration; court accepts 
proportional downgrade.   
- **Loss Conditions:** Identification admitted and reliable; 
prosecution shows sustained/targeted conduct; medical supports 
repeated/targeted blows; CCTV shows prolonged attack; weapon use shows 
targeting/duration; court rejects challenges.   
- **Procedural Actions:** Request Turnbull direction; challenge CCTV 
quality for identification; chase disclosure with timetable; seek 
directions if missed; full CCTV export + continuity; complete MG6C; 
forensic methodology + chain; medical mechanism clarification; 
phone/message disclosure. 
 
--- 
 
## 20 Defence Case Statement 
- **Primary Issue:** Identification reliability — Turnbull risk. 
Conditions were poor (lighting variable, distance, brief duration 
~15–30s, hood obstruction throughout, witness uncertainty, similar 
clothing on others, CCTV quality insufficient for facial 
identification). Defence will challenge identification and seek 
Turnbull direction. If identification is unreliable or excluded, case 
fails.   
- **Secondary Issues:** If identification admitted, then intent 
threshold (s18 vs s20), sequence/duration (brief), forensic weight 
(partial mixed DNA), disclosure completeness.   
- **Position:** Identification is unreliable and should be excluded or 
heavily qualified under Turnbull. If identification is admitted, harm 
accepted but intent not at s18 threshold; circumstances support 
s20/lesser; seek charge review/downgrade as fallback. 
 
--- 
 
## 21 PTPH Case Management Note 

- PTPH 04 Sep 2024: Plea Not Guilty to s18. Defence primary position: 
identification unreliable (Turnbull challenge). Fallback: contests 
intent; seeks reduction to s20 if identification admitted.   
- Disclosure outstanding: MG6C incomplete; CCTV continuity; phone data; 
forensic methodology; full CCTV quality assessment for identification 
purposes.   
- Directions requested: Turnbull direction on identification; 
completion by 15 Sep; charge review; possible defence medical expert; 
trial window after disclosure. 
 
--- 
 
## 22 Bail Conditions Summary 
- Bailed 13 Aug; conditions: no contact with complainant; exclusion 
zone around Blue Lantern; reside at 12 Fiction Close; surrender 
passport; attend court; no further offences.   
- Bail continued at PTPH; no breaches reported. 
 
--- 
 
## 23 Draft Skeleton Argument – Charge Reduction 
- Framework: s18 requires specific intent; s20 does not.   
- Submissions: brief/chaotic 15–30s; no sustained/targeted conduct; 
medical single-motion ambiguity; weapon presence alone not intent; 
partial DNA non-exclusive; ID poor.   
- Proportional case management: invite s18 → s20; not a concession; 
reflects evidential intent contestability.

11A Turnbull Identification Assessment (Supplemental) 
Case Ref: CRN-TEST-8742 | URN: URN-23-TEST-4411   
Assessment Date: 30 August 2024 
 
Identification Conditions Summary 
Lighting: Variable; streetlights and takeaway window lighting; 
areas of shadow; not optimal for facial identification.   
Distance: Witnesses at 3–50 metres; door staff at ~50m; 
complainant at close range but brief exposure.   
Duration: Incident visible for 15–30 seconds; identification 
window brief.   
Obstruction: Attacker wore dark hooded top with hood up 
throughout; facial features not clearly visible in any CCTV still or 
witness account.   
Angle: CCTV angles partial; signage and camera positioning limit 
facial visibility; back/side views primarily.   
Similarity: Multiple individuals in area wearing similar dark 
clothing; no distinctive features reliably distinguishing attacker from 
others. 
 
Turnbull Risk Factors 
1. Poor viewing conditions: Lighting variable, distance, brief 
duration.   
2. Obstruction: Hood worn throughout; no clear facial view.   
3. Witness uncertainty: All witnesses express uncertainty; CCTV 
stills show similarity but not certainty.   
4. Similar clothing: Other individuals in area wearing similar dark 
clothing.   
5. No distinctive features: No reliable distinguishing features 
visible in available evidence. 
 
CCTV Quality Assessment (Facial Identification) 
Facial visibility: Poor to non-existent across all cameras due to 
hood, angle, and lighting.   
Identification reliability: CCTV footage is unreliable for 
positive identification purposes. Facial features are not clearly 

visible; identification would require inference from clothing and 
general build, which is insufficient for Turnbull compliance.   
Use of CCTV: CCTV may assist with sequence/duration assessment 
but does not support reliable identification of the individual 
involved. 
 
Conclusion 
Identification evidence presents Turnbull risk. Conditions were poor 
(lighting, distance, duration, obstruction). Witnesses express 
uncertainty. CCTV does not provide reliable facial identification. 
Defence will challenge identification reliability and seek Turnbull 
direction.
